newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon's Byblos Bank profits up 60 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon's Byblos Bank profits up 60 pct in 1996.

text.p: Byblos Bank, which plans to list 30 percent of its shares shortly on the Beirut Stock Exchange, reported on Wednesday that profits rose 60 percent in 1996 to $24 million.
It said it achieved record results for the fourth consecutive year and continued to record growth rates that outperformed the Lebanese banking sector.
Profits per share rose to $0.60 from $0.36, it said.

Total assets rose 38 percent to $1.430 billion, customer deposits rose 35 percent to $1.179 billion and capital was increased to $105 million from $73 million, according to the bank's audited results.

(Note: Cooke Ratio includes retained net income of the year.)
Byblos is considered one of Lebanon's most dynamic banks. It said its growth in customer deposits in 1996 raised it to fifth place among Lebanon's 82 banks from seventh place in 1995.
According to the Almanac of the Lebanese Banks Association, Byblos Bank has 27 branches in Lebanon and an offshore branch in Cyprus. It has 579 employees.
